body: An artist’s concept depicting a Voyager spacecraft. Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech Launched nearly 50 years ago in 1977, NASA’s Voyager 1 on Wednesday, Nov. 18 will have traveled one light-day from Earth, which is more than 16 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object, and any light from Earth would take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft. NASA will highlight this historic milestone with two events. On Tuesday, Nov. 17, NASA invites the world to participate in “Shine Bright for Voyager’s Light-Day” by creating a symbolic wave of golden light encircling the planet after sunset. NASA has created a website that enables smart phones and tablets to flash “VGR”, Voyager’s call sign, in morse code. For more information about how to participate in “Shine Bright for Voyager Light-Day,” visit: go.nasa.gov/shinebright Everyone is encouraged to capture photos or videos of their light-day signal and share it on social platforms, tagging @NASA. title: Google Wallet gets Alipay Plus support with Traveler QR
summary: The system extends payment support across merchants in Southeast Asia.
body: TL;DR Last month, we spotted Google Wallet working on support for “Traveler QR.” That’s now arriving with this week’s Google Play services update. The system supports payments through Alipay Plus in Southeast Asia. Last month, we spotted Google working on “ Traveler QR ,” a new Wallet payment option for the Alipay Plus network in Southeast Asia, and now it looks like it’s finally arriving. Google Play services version 26.44 starts heading out to Android users today, and in its release notes , Google shares that Traveler QR support is going live in Wallet. We already saw Google’s Traveler QR documentation appear online, and it felt like just a matter of time before the feature would get its official debut.
